title: Three-dimensional volumetric analysis of mandibular condyle changes in active growing condylar hyperplasia
html: Condylar hyperplasia is characterized by excessive mandibular condylar growth, causing progressive facial asymmetry and occlusal discrepancies. This study investigates the transition from active to inactive growth stages, a critical determinant for optimizing surgical timing and selecting appropriate intervals for corrective orthognathic surgery. A retrospective study was conducted involving 30 patients with unilateral condylar hyperplasia (mean age 21.90 ± 4.16 years) at a university hospital. Assessment of condylar hyperplasia involved measuring metabolic activity through bone scintigraphy, in conjunction with three-dimensional volumetric and height evaluations via computed tomography (CT).
